findings.title: Case-sensitive email lookup allows bypassing blocked emails
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` without normalizing or downcasing `email`, and `BlockedEmail` does not downcase `email` before saving either. Because `User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` directly without downcasing and PostgreSQL string comparisons on `varchar` are case-sensitive, a user whose address is stored in `blocked_emails` as `bad@spammers.org` can bypass the block by signing up with `Bad@spammers.org`.

findings.title: Mutating `BlockedEmail#match_count` inside validator double-counts on signup
findings.body: `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, which increments `match_count` and saves the `BlockedEmail` record every time validations run. In `UsersController#create` (lines 168-172), `user.valid?` is evaluated first in `if user.valid? && SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` and then `user.save` runs validations a second time (after clearing `user.errors`), causing `BlockedEmail.should_block?` to execute twice and increment `match_count` by 2 for a single signup attempt.
